statement: Using the following definitions, the function returns a result r and r is the exact maximum. For a byte string x of length n, x is a palindrome iff for every q with 0 <= q < n, x[q] = x[n-1-q] (so empty and length-one strings are palindromes). For indices 0 <= i <= j <= len(s), s[i..j] denotes the contiguous substring of s of length j-i whose p-th byte, for 0 <= p < j-i, is s[i+p]; s[i..i] is empty. Similarly t[k..l] for 0 <= k <= l <= len(t). Then r is the greatest integer m for which there exist 0 <= i <= j <= len(s) and 0 <= k <= l <= len(t) such that the concatenation s[i..j] ++ t[k..l] is a palindrome and m = (j-i)+(l-k).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: For every s and t satisfying the preconditions, the function terminates successfully and returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= len(s) + len(t).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= 1.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there exist indices 0 <= i <= j <= len(s) and 0 <= k <= l <= len(t) such that s[i..j] ++ t[k..l] is a palindrome and (j-i)+(l-k) = r.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every choice of indices 0 <= i <= j <= len(s) and 0 <= k <= l <= len(t), if s[i..j] ++ t[k..l] is a palindrome, then (j-i)+(l-k) <= r.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r >= max(LPS(s), LPS(t)), where for a byte slice x, LPS(x) is the greatest length of a contiguous substring of x that is a palindrome (equivalently, the greatest (j-i) with 0 <= i <= j <= len(x) and x[i..j] a palindrome; empty substrings are allowed, so LPS(x) >= 0).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 2 if s[0] = t[0], and r = 1 otherwise.
preconditions: len(s) = 1, len(t) = 1, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(s) + len(t).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122, and there exists a byte c such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] = c, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(t), t[j] = c.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = max(len(s), len(t)).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122, and there exist bytes a and b with a != b such that for every i with 0 <= i < len(s), s[i] = a, and for every j with 0 <= j < len(t), t[j] = b.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122, and all bytes occurring in s and t are pairwise distinct: for every 0 <= i < len(s) and 0 <= j < len(t), s[i] != t[j]; for every 0 <= i < i' < len(s), s[i] != s[i']; and for every 0 <= j < j' < len(t), t[j] != t[j'].

statement: Let rev(x) denote the byte slice obtained by reversing x. Whenever the function returns r on inputs (s,t), the function on inputs (rev(t), rev(s)) (which also satisfies the preconditions) returns the same value r; equivalently, r(s,t) = r(rev(t), rev(s)).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(s) + len(t) if and only if the full concatenation s[0..len(s)] ++ t[0..len(t)] (i.e., s followed by t) is a palindrome.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(t) >= 1, len(s) <= 1000, len(t) <= 1000, and every byte of s and every byte of t is one of the lowercase English letters 97 through 122.

statement: For any such s,t,s',t', whenever the function returns r on (s,t) and r' on (s',t'), r <= r'.
preconditions: s,t,s',t' all satisfy the same constraints: lengths between 1 and 1000, and all bytes are lowercase English letters 97 through 122. Moreover, s occurs as a contiguous substring of s', and t occurs as a contiguous substring of t'.
